generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, the three strands run together as you move through placements, practicals and supervised work. You own an experience, such as running a session or a client interaction, carry it through the cycle so the reflection is critical, then write it up for a portfolio or supervision log. Done after each one, with a change carried forward, the rounds build your practice over the course.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two trainees get the same supervisor feedback on an early case write-up. One moves straight to the next case and repeats the same thin analysis. The other owns it, runs the case through the cycle, writes an evaluation linking it to theory, and changes how she prepares. Over the placement her case work improves, because the three strands ran as one practice.
generatedProse.summary: In psychology, reflective practice matters most when the three strands run as one. You own each placement or practical experience, work it through the cycle, and write an evaluation that justifies a change. It is the repeated practice, not one reflection, that builds you as a practitioner.

check.body: A newly qualified practitioner owns a difficult episode, runs it through the cycle to reach a change, writes it up as an evaluation, and applies the change next time. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first report, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next report.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next report, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next report improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That the three strands work as one practice: the stance, the cycle and the writing together produced a change that improved the next experience.
_items.feedback: Yes. The whole loop ran: own it, reflect critically, write the evaluation, carry the change forward.

_items.text: That the practitioner simply described the episode in more detail than before.
_items.feedback: Describing is only the start. Here the practitioner evaluated and changed, which is the practice.

_items.text: That writing the reflection down was the only part that mattered.
_items.feedback: The writing records the work, but the stance and the cycle did the reflecting first.

_items.text: That the episode would now never happen again.
_items.feedback: Reflection does not guarantee that. It changes how you act and keep developing.
